Preparation of 2,2,2-Trifluoro-1-(p-tolyl)ethanol23 (2a). The following is a modification of the procedure outlined by Kelly et al.24 To a 100 mL round-bottom flask equipped with a stir bar was added THF (24 mL), p-tolualdehyde (2.723 g, 0.020 mol, 0.83 M, 1 equiv), and (trifluoromethyl)- trimethylsilane (3.12 g, 0.022 mol, 1.3 equiv). The flask was sealed with a rubber septum and placed under a N2 atmosphere via an inlet needle. The reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice-water bath and stirred via a magnetic stir plate. After approximately 10 min, TBAF (1 M in THF, 0.2 mL, 0.0002 mol, 0.01 equiv) was added dropwise via a syringe. Note: on small scales, i.e. <20 mmol, the TBAF could be added relatively quickly. However, upon scale-up the addition of TBAF is quite exothermic. Hence, it is recommended that the TBAF be added as slowly as possible and/or the reaction mixture be cooled to a temperature lower than 0 °C. After 10 min, the ice bath was removed and the solution was stirred for approximately 6 h at room temperature. To cleave the silyl ether intermediate, the reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice bath. After 10 min, water (2 mL, 0.110 mol, 5.5 equiv) was added via a syringe. TBAF (1 M in THF, 2 mL, 0.002 mol, 0.1 equiv) was then added. After 10 min the ice bath was removed and the reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature. When the cleavage was judged to be complete (determined by GC-MS or NMR), the contents of the flask were transferred to a separatory funnel. Note: some of the silyl ethers were very slow to cleave and required another addition of TBAF and water. Brine (~100mL) and Et2O (~150mL) were added, and the layers were partitioned. The aqueous layer was back-extracted (3 × ~50mL) with Et2O. The combined ether layers were dried with Na2SO4, and the solvent was removed in vacuo via rotary evaporation to afford crude 2, which was further purified by vacuum distillation to give the pure α -CF3 alcohol 2. 1,1,1-Trifluoroundec-10-en-2-ol (2m). Preparation of 2,2,2-Trifluoro-1-(p-tolyl)ethanol23 (2a). The following is a modification of the procedure outlined by Kelly et al.24 To a 100 mL round-bottom flask equipped with a stir bar was added THF (24 mL), p-tolualdehyde (2.723 g, 0.020 mol, 0.83 M, 1 equiv), and (trifluoromethyl)- trimethylsilane (3.12 g, 0.022 mol, 1.3 equiv). The flask was sealed with a rubber septum and placed under a N2 atmosphere via an inlet needle. The reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice-water bath and stirred via a magnetic stir plate. After approximately 10 min, TBAF (1 M in THF, 0.2 mL, 0.0002 mol, 0.01 equiv) was added dropwise via a syringe. Note: on small scales, i.e. <20 mmol, the TBAF could be added relatively quickly. However, upon scale-up the addition of TBAF is quite exothermic. Hence, it is recommended that the TBAF be added as slowly as possible and/or the reaction mixture be cooled to a temperature lower than 0 °C. After 10 min, the ice bath was removed and the solution was stirred for approximately 6 h at room temperature. To cleave the silyl ether intermediate, the reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice bath. After 10 min, water (2 mL, 0.110 mol, 5.5 equiv) was added via a syringe. TBAF (1 M in THF, 2 mL, 0.002 mol, 0.1 equiv) was then added. After 10 min the ice bath was removed and the reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature. When the cleavage was judged to be complete (determined by GC-MS or NMR), the contents of the flask were transferred to a separatory funnel. Note: some of the silyl ethers were very slow to cleave and required another addition of TBAF and water. Brine (~100mL) and Et2O (~150mL) were added, and the layers were partitioned. The aqueous layer was back-extracted (3 × ~50mL) with Et2O. After approximately 10 min, TBAF (1 M in THF, 0.2 mL, 0.0002 mol, 0.01 equiv) was added dropwise via a syringe. Note: on small scales, i.e. <20 mmol, the TBAF could be added relatively quickly. A 100 mL, 3-necked, round-bottomed flask was equipped with a gas inlet, a stopper, and a septum. The flask was charged with 5.1 g (0.027 mol 1.28 equiv) of TMS-CF2CF3, 3.0g (0.021 mol, 1 equiv) of 6, and 25 mL of THF. Under argon, the stirred mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice-water bath, stirred for 5 minutes, and TBAF (0.22 mL, 0.00022 mol, 1M in THF and 5% w/w. H2O, 0.01 equiv) was then syringed into the mixture, whereupon immediate gas evolution was noted and the solution became a dark brownish-orange color. The ice bath was removed, and the mixture was allowed to warm to room temperature, while stirring. After 3 hours, GC-MS confirmed complete reaction of the starting material to the intermediate silyl ether. In order to cleave the intermediate silyl ether, the flask was placed in an ice-bath for five minutes, and 2.0 mL (0.11 mol, 5.24 equiv) of H2O and an additional 1.3 mL of TBAF solution (0.0013 mol, 1M in THF and 5% w/w. H2O, 0.062 equiv) were added via syringe. The flask was removed from the ice-bath and allowed to stir overnight, whereupon GC-MS indicated complete conversion to 7b. Upon completion, approximately 1 gram of solid sodium chloride was added to the reaction mixture and it was briefly stirred to assist separation of the THF from the water. Solid NaCl remained in the bottom of the flask. The stirrer was shut off, and the liquid was decanted into a separatory funnel, along with 75 mL of ether, using some of the ether to rinse the salt left in the flask. The mixture was then washed with brine ( 1 X 50 mL), and the two layers separated. The brine layer was back-extracted with additional ether (3 X 25 mL), and these extracts were added to the first organic layer. The combined organic layers were dried with Na2SO4 and filtered through filter paper into a round bottom flask, using pentane to rinse the Na2SO4. The solvent was removed in vacuo via rotary evaporation yielding a thick orange-brown oil. The crude product was purified by vacuum distillation (bp 80-85 °C @ 30 mm Hg) to give 7b as a white crystalline solid. During vacuum distillation, the product was observed to solidify in and clog the condenser, even when 45 °C water was circulated through it using a submersible pump (as described for 7a). Consequently, it was necessary to remove the water from the condenser (using air cooling only), and heat it periodically with a heat gun during the distillation to melt the solid down into the receiving cow. The flask was sealed with a rubber septum and placed under a N2 atmosphere via an inlet needle. The reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice-water bath and stirred via a magnetic stir plate. After approximately 10 min, TBAF (1 M in THF, 0.2 mL, 0.0002 mol, 0.01 equiv) was added dropwise via a syringe. Note: on small scales, i.e. <20 mmol, the TBAF could be added relatively quickly. However, upon scale-up the addition of TBAF is quite exothermic. Hence, it is recommended that the TBAF be added as slowly as possible and/or the reaction mixture be cooled to a temperature lower than 0 °C. After 10 min, the ice bath was removed and the solution was stirred for approximately 6 h at room temperature. To cleave the silyl ether intermediate, the reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice bath. After 10 min, water (2 mL, 0.110 mol, 5.5 equiv) was added via a syringe. TBAF (1 M in THF, 2 mL, 0.002 mol, 0.1 equiv) was then added. After 10 min the ice bath was removed and the reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature. When the cleavage was judged to be complete (determined by GC-MS or NMR), the contents of the flask were transferred to a separatory funnel. Note: some of the silyl ethers were very slow to cleave and required another addition of TBAF and water. Brine (~100mL) and Et2O (~150mL) were added, and the layers were partitioned. The aqueous layer was back-extracted (3 × ~50mL) with Et2O. The combined ether layers were dried with Na2SO4, and the solvent was removed in vacuo via rotary evaporation to afford crude 2, which was further purified by vacuum distillation to give the pure α -CF3 alcohol 2. 1,1,1-Trifluoro-4-(furan-2-yl)but-3-en-2-ol (2s). Preparation of 2,2,2-Trifluoro-1-(p-tolyl)ethanol23 (2a). The following is a modification of the procedure outlined by Kelly et al.24 To a 100 mL round-bottom flask equipped with a stir bar was added THF (24 mL), p-tolualdehyde (2.723 g, 0.020 mol, 0.83 M, 1 equiv), and (trifluoromethyl)- trimethylsilane (3.12 g, 0.022 mol, 1.3 equiv). The flask was sealed with a rubber septum and placed under a N2 atmosphere via an inlet needle. The reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice-water bath and stirred via a magnetic stir plate. After approximately 10 min, TBAF (1 M in THF, 0.2 mL, 0.0002 mol, 0.01 equiv) was added dropwise via a syringe. Note: on small scales, i.e. <20 mmol, the TBAF could be added relatively quickly. However, upon scale-up the addition of TBAF is quite exothermic. Hence, it is recommended that the TBAF be added as slowly as possible and/or the reaction mixture be cooled to a temperature lower than 0 °C. After 10 min, the ice bath was removed and the solution was stirred for approximately 6 h at room temperature. To cleave the silyl ether intermediate, the reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice bath. After 10 min, water (2 mL, 0.110 mol, 5.5 equiv) was added via a syringe. TBAF (1 M in THF, 2 mL, 0.002 mol, 0.1 equiv) was then added. After 10 min the ice bath was removed and the reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature. When the cleavage was judged to be complete (determined by GC-MS or NMR), the contents of the flask were transferred to a separatory funnel. Note: some of the silyl ethers were very slow to cleave and required another addition of TBAF and water. Brine (~100mL) and Et2O (~150mL) were added, and the layers were partitioned. The aqueous layer was back-extracted (3 × ~50mL) with Et2O. The combined ether layers were dried with Na2SO4, and the solvent was removed in vacuo via rotary evaporation to afford crude 2, which was further purified by vacuum distillation to give the pure α -CF3 alcohol 2. 2,2,2-Trifluoro-1-(2-methoxyphenyl)ethanol (2i). The title compound (3.520 g, 85%) was prepared according to the representative procedure from o-methoxybenzaldehyde (2.720 g, 0.020 mol) followed by vacuum distillation to give the pure α -CF3 alcohol 2i as a clear colorless oil. The following is a modification of the procedure outlined by Kelly et al.24 To a 100 mL round-bottom flask equipped with a stir bar was added THF (24 mL), p-tolualdehyde (2.723 g, 0.020 mol, 0.83 M, 1 equiv), and (trifluoromethyl)- trimethylsilane (3.12 g, 0.022 mol, 1.3 equiv). The flask was sealed with a rubber septum and placed under a N2 atmosphere via an inlet needle. The reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice-water bath and stirred via a magnetic stir plate. After approximately 10 min, TBAF (1 M in THF, 0.2 mL, 0.0002 mol, 0.01 equiv) was added dropwise via a syringe. Note: on small scales, i.e. <20 mmol, the TBAF could be added relatively quickly. However, upon scale-up the addition of TBAF is quite exothermic. Hence, it is recommended that the TBAF be added as slowly as possible and/or the reaction mixture be cooled to a temperature lower than 0 °C. After 10 min, the ice bath was removed and the solution was stirred for approximately 6 h at room temperature. To cleave the silyl ether intermediate, the reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice bath. After 10 min, water (2 mL, 0.110 mol, 5.5 equiv) was added via a syringe. TBAF (1 M in THF, 2 mL, 0.002 mol, 0.1 equiv) was then added. After 10 min the ice bath was removed and the reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature. When the cleavage was judged to be complete (determined by GC-MS or NMR), the contents of the flask were transferred to a separatory funnel. Note: some of the silyl ethers were very slow to cleave and required another addition of TBAF and water. Brine (~100mL) and Et2O (~150mL) were added, and the layers were partitioned. The aqueous layer was back-extracted (3 × ~50mL) with Et2O. The combined ether layers were dried with Na2SO4, and the solvent was removed in vacuo via rotary evaporation to afford crude 2, which was further purified by vacuum distillation to give the pure α -CF3 alcohol 2. 2,2,2-Trifluoro-1-(p-tolyl)ethanol25 (2a). Preparation of 2,2,2-Trifluoro-1-(p-tolyl)ethanol23 (2a). The following is a modification of the procedure outlined by Kelly et al.24 To a 100 mL round-bottom flask equipped with a stir bar was added THF (24 mL), p-tolualdehyde (2.723 g, 0.020 mol, 0.83 M, 1 equiv), and (trifluoromethyl)- trimethylsilane (3.12 g, 0.022 mol, 1.3 equiv). The flask was sealed with a rubber septum and placed under a N2 atmosphere via an inlet needle. The reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice-water bath and stirred via a magnetic stir plate. After approximately 10 min, TBAF (1 M in THF, 0.2 mL, 0.0002 mol, 0.01 equiv) was added dropwise via a syringe. Note: on small scales, i.e. <20 mmol, the TBAF could be added relatively quickly. However, upon scale-up the addition of TBAF is quite exothermic. Hence, it is recommended that the TBAF be added as slowly as possible and/or the reaction mixture be cooled to a temperature lower than 0 °C. After 10 min, the ice bath was removed and the solution was stirred for approximately 6 h at room temperature. To cleave the silyl ether intermediate, the reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice bath. After 10 min, water (2 mL, 0.110 mol, 5.5 equiv) was added via a syringe. TBAF (1 M in THF, 2 mL, 0.002 mol, 0.1 equiv) was then added. After 10 min the ice bath was removed and the reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature. When the cleavage was judged to be complete (determined by GC-MS or NMR), the contents of the flask were transferred to a separatory funnel. Note: some of the silyl ethers were very slow to cleave and required another addition of TBAF and water. Brine (~100mL) and Et2O (~150mL) were added, and the layers were partitioned. The aqueous layer was back-extracted (3 × ~50mL) with Et2O. The combined ether layers were dried with Na2SO4, and the solvent was removed in vacuo via rotary evaporation to afford crude 2, which was further purified by vacuum distillation to give the pure α -CF3 alcohol 2. 1-(2-Bromo-4-fluorophenyl)-2,2,2-trifluoroethanol26 (2f).
